title: sse: fix partial-JSON delimiter ordering and token/event framing
author: Emily Chen
description:
Motivation: several production incidents (INC-2026-02, tracked in ENG-3241) exposed an edge case in the SSE streaming path where partial JSON payloads emitted across chunk boundaries could be re-ordered at the token/event layer, resulting in syntactically invalid partial-json events or swapped delimiter tokens. This caused downstream clients that parse partial JSON (structured output mode) to see malformed objects or to drop function/tool-calling events. This PR stabilizes the SSE chunking/framing state machine to enforce deterministic ordering of delimiter tokens, partial-json fragments, and synthetic events (e.g. [DONE]/[DELIM]).

Summary of changes: 1) introduce an explicit framing queue between the tokenizer and SSE emitter to preserve event order when flushes and buffer boundaries occur; 2) add a small finite-state machine (FSM) to guarantee that partial-json delimiter tokens are emitted in the correct order with respect to their surrounding JSON tokens; 3) update the OpenAI-compat layer to coalesce function-call or tool events that were susceptible to being split into out-of-order fragments; 4) add unit and integration tests covering previously flaky ordering cases and add a deterministic replication test used in incidents.

Checklist: - [x] Add framing FSM and unit tests - [x] Add integration tests with streaming partial JSON scenarios - [x] Add compatibility coalescing for OpenAI-compat tool/function events - [x] Run perf microbenchmarks to ensure no regression in median latency - [x] Update changelog and release notes section below

Related: Linear ENG-3241 (incident replication), ENG-3270 (streaming stability epic). This PR is focused and backwards-compatible: consumers unchanged unless they depended on previous malformed ordering (which was a bug).

review_conversation: Marcus Lee: Can you explain why we need an explicit queue vs forcing flushing order at the tokenizer?

Emily Chen: The tokenizer emits async flushes from multiple stages (prefix cache, KV cache, decoding). The explicit queue centralizes ordering guarantees and is the smallest surface change to prevent reordering without altering tokenizer internals.
Ravi Shah: The FSM looks good. Please add comments for the state transitions and a small diagram in the file header.
Emily Chen: Added comments and ascii diagram in framing_fsm.go head. Also expanded unit tests to cover transition table.
Santiago Ruiz: Observability: add a metric for 'sse_framing_reorders' (should be 0) so we can detect regressions in prod.
Emily Chen: Added 'sse_framing_reorders' and a debug log emitted at level DEBUG when a reorder would have occurred (should never fire after this PR).
release_notes: Fix: SSE streaming partial-JSON delimiter ordering and token/event framing. This resolves cases where partial JSON or function/tool events could be emitted out-of-order, causing client parsing failures. No breaking changes expected.
